validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE (high): confirmed via an independent, authoritative primary source outside the sheet's own citation chain -- the World Bank's 1997 Implementation Completion Report for the 'Fourth and Kureimat Power Projects' (Loans 3103 and 3441-EGT), downloaded and read with pdftotext (the page-fetch/url_verifier substring check FAILs on this 3.8MB scanned PDF -- a documented large-PDF false-negative already noted in this PID's own RouteNotes -- so I verified manually: fetched the PDF directly, ran pdftotext, and grepped the output; the sentence is there verbatim, line 853 of the extracted text). Para 4.4 states: 'the Bank funded the foreign costs for 95 km of the 22-inch diameter El Tebbin (Dahsour) to Kureimat natural gas pipeline, which was to be funded by EGPC.' Para 3.8 (per this PID's own prior-pass RouteNotes, which I re-verified) adds the completion date: 'the El Tebbin-Kureimat pipeline is scheduled for completion in September 1996.' That is a real, funded, physically-built gas pipeline distinct from a same-named electricity transmission line a prior pass had correctly ruled out -- not a GEM-only entity. CLASSIFICATION (high): correctly PipelineType=transmission -- it is a foreign-financed trunk line feeding a 1,200 MW power station's gas supply as part of the national grid, not a local distribution main; Fuel=Gas is explicit in the WB doc ('natural gas pipeline') and independently corroborated by both endpoint facilities' own fuel-type listings (ueepc.com Kureimat page: 'نوع الوقود: غاز طبيعى / مازوت' / natural gas-fuel oil; cairoepc.com Tebbin page: same wording) -- both verified live via url_verifier. DUPLICATE watchlist question (resolved, high confidence): is this a segment of the same Suez-to-Cairo trunk as P8014 'Zaafarana-Kuraimat'? NO -- the same WB paragraph distinguishes them explicitly and gives materially different specs: 'the diameter of the 160-km pipeline from Zafarana to Kureimat was changed from 20 inches to 18 inches' (i.e. P8014, matches GEM's 163km/18in closely) versus the 95km/22-inch El Tebbin-Kureimat line (this row, P8021). Different origin, different diameter (18in vs 22in), different foreign financing arrangement -- two real, distinct pipelines that happen to share Kuraimat as a hub, not a double-count. STATUS=operating (medium-high): no source explicitly labels current-day status, but the pipeline was scheduled for completion in Sept 1996 (per the WB ICR) and appears as a green ('Existing P/L' per the legend) line on the 2018 GASCO National Gas Grid map (EGAS Annual Report 2018, p.35) -- ~30 years of service with no closure/cancellation signal found; operating is the reasonable read. MAP TEST APPLIED (per scope guidance): the sheet's own cited EGAS Annual Report 2018 PDF fails a full-text search for 'Kuraimat' (confirmed: url_verifier FAILs the token), but per this cohort's known pattern I read the actual GASCO national-grid MAP on p.35 (cached at batches/egypt-gas/archive/staging/route-creation-20260807/maps/egas2018_p35_gasco_national_grid.png from a prior pass) rather than relying on the miss. The map shows a green line running Tebbin -> Dahshour -> Koraimat with two inline labels stacked along that exact corridor: '32" 70 k.m' (a separate line -- matches the map's own text callout 'New Capital / Dahshour Pipeline 70 km - 32", Completed July 2017', i.e. a DIFFERENT pipeline, not this row) and, directly below it toward Koraimat, '22" 87 k.m' -- an exact match to this row's Diameter (22in) and Length (87.00km). So the existing Length/Diameter refs ARE genuinely supported by the cited document, just via its map rather than its text -- the full-text miss is not evidence of a bad citation here, confirming the scope's standing caution. DIAMETER (high, 2 independent sources agree exactly): 22in per both the GASCO map label and the WB ICR text ('22-inch diameter El Tebbin ... to Kureimat'). LOCATION/geography (confirmed): Kuraimat/Kureimat village sits in Giza Governorate ~90km south of Cairo on the Nile's west bank (matches StartState/Province=Giza); Al Tebbin is a district of southern Cairo/Helwan in Cairo Governorate (matches EndState/Province=Cairo). The routes-repo geometry for this PID (RouteAccuracy='very low (straight line/schematic)') runs from ~29.285N,31.244E (Kuraimat) to ~29.776N,31.298E (Tebbin) -- both coordinates land on the correct real-world places, consistent with the WB/map sourcing above. Note the merged route's own geodesic length is only ~55km against the schematic's 4 vertices (it follows a straight desert-edge chord, not the river's actual course) -- expected for a 'very low' schematic route and not itself a new finding; already the documented state of this PID's RouteAccuracy.
